reference: GNU coreutils ln, with exact stdout/status and private filesystem bytes, modes, hardlink relationships and symlink targets. Bash type/help checks are metadata contracts.
coverage: Hard links, relative and dangling symlinks, multiple operands, collisions, force replacement, spaced names and missing operands.
Single-operand destination, -- and dash names, symlink replacement, partial failure and repeated calls.
Bash registration and help metadata; separately identified from operations.
exclusions: Interactive prompting and filesystem fault injection are outside this bounded suite; no privileged operation is needed for ordinary links.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash resolves ln as a builtin with the executable search path empty, using the documented type -t classification.
cases.script: PATH=; type -t ln

cases.purpose: Confirm help exposes the documented short usage string registered for ln without invoking the loadable operation. The synopsis lists the GNU options ln gained in guest compatibility pass 1.
cases.script: PATH=; help -s ln

cases.purpose: Create a hard link; compare bytes, modes, link count and inode relationship.
cases.script:
printf 'link bytes\n' > source
ln source destination
[[ source -ef destination ]]
stat -c '%h' source

cases.purpose: Preserve the relative symlink target and read through it from its parent directory.
cases.script:
mkdir data links
printf 'relative bytes\n' > data/item
ln -s ../data/item links/current
readlink links/current
cat links/current

cases.purpose: A dangling symbolic link succeeds and preserves its literal target.
cases.script:
ln -s future-name dangling
[[ -L dangling && ! -e dangling ]]
readlink dangling

cases.purpose: Create multiple relative symlinks into an existing directory and compare followed bytes and stored targets.
cases.script:
mkdir output
printf one > one
printf two > two
(cd output; ln -s ../one ../two .)
cat output/one output/two

cases.purpose: An existing destination is preserved on failure, including both original file payloads.
cases.script:
printf original > source
printf keep > destination
ln source destination

cases.purpose: Replace only the private destination with a hard link and compare its resulting tree.
cases.script:
printf original > source
printf replace > destination
ln -f source destination
[[ source -ef destination ]]

cases.purpose: Quoted operand boundaries survive hard-link creation.
cases.script:
printf bytes > 'source with space'
ln 'source with space' 'destination with space'
[[ 'source with space' -ef 'destination with space' ]]

cases.purpose: Compare missing-operand status and diagnostic presence without mutating the fixture.
cases.script: ln

cases.purpose: A single source operand creates its basename in the current private directory.
cases.script:
mkdir origin dest
printf item > origin/item
(cd dest; ln ../origin/item)
[[ origin/item -ef dest/item ]]

cases.purpose: Use -- with a dash-leading source and replace a private dangling symlink with -sf.
cases.script:
printf x > -source
ln -- -source hard
ln -s stale symbolic
ln -sf -- -source symbolic
readlink symbolic

cases.purpose: Compare aggregate failure status and successful middle link amid two missing sources.
cases.script:
mkdir dest
printf x > good
ln absent good missing dest

cases.purpose: Compare ln hardlink/symlink effects within a private tree assembled with ordinary GNU file operations; also preserve bytes and modes through the surrounding copy/move/removal steps.
cases.script:
mkdir -p -- alpha/sub
printf 'fixture data\n' > alpha/sub/source
ln -- alpha/sub/source alpha/hard
ln -s -- sub/source alpha/symbolic
cp -- alpha/sub/source alpha/copy
chmod 640 alpha/copy
mv -- alpha/copy alpha/moved
touch -- alpha/stamp
touch -- alpha/remove-me
rm -- alpha/remove-me

cases.purpose: Compare ln hardlink/symlink effects within a private tree assembled with ordinary GNU file operations; also preserve bytes and modes through the surrounding copy/move/removal steps.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/src tree/dst
touch tree/src/original tree/to-remove
printf 'payload\n' > tree/src/original
chmod 640 tree/src/original
cp -p tree/src/original tree/copied
ln tree/src/original tree/hard
ln -s src/original tree/symbolic
mv tree/copied tree/dst/copied
rm tree/to-remove
touch tree/dst/touched
chmod 600 tree/dst/touched
printf 'fixture-ready\n'

cases.purpose: Compare ln hardlink/symlink effects within a private tree assembled with ordinary GNU file operations; also preserve bytes and modes through the surrounding copy/move/removal steps.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/nested
printf 'one\n' > source/nested/item
cp -R source copied
mv copied moved
chmod 700 moved
rm -r source
printf 'recursive-fixture-ready\n'
ln moved/nested/item linked-item
[[ moved/nested/item -ef linked-item ]]

cases.purpose: The documented -n option replaces a symlink to a directory instead of following it when combined with -f.
cases.script:
mkdir target
printf data > source
ln -s target destination
ln -fn source destination
[[ source -ef destination && ! -L destination ]]

cases.purpose: -r/--relative makes the symlink target relative to the link's directory (guest compatibility pass 1).
cases.script:
mkdir -p a/b c/d
printf x > a/b/f
ln -sr a/b/f c/d/l1
readlink c/d/l1
ln -s --relative a/b/f l2
readlink l2
ln -sr a/b a/b2
readlink a/b2
ln -sr c/d/l1 c/l3
readlink c/l3
cat c/d/l1 l2
ln -r a/b/f nos || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: -t DIR links each TARGET into DIR; -T treats LINK_NAME as a file even when it is a directory.
cases.script:
mkdir dir other
printf 1 > one; printf 2 > two
ln -t dir one two
[[ one -ef dir/one && two -ef dir/two ]] && echo t-ok
ln --target-directory=other -s ../one
readlink other/one
ln -T one other || echo rc=$?
ln -sT one newname && readlink newname
ln -t dir -T one x || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: -v prints each link; -b and --backup=numbered keep the replaced destination.
cases.script:
printf a > a; printf b > b; printf c > c
ln -sv a s1
ln -sfvb b s1
readlink s1 s1~
ln -f --backup=numbered c b
ln -f --backup=numbered a b
ls b b.~1~ b.~2~
ln -S .old -fb c a
ls a a.old

cases.purpose: Unknown options, --relative without --symbolic and missing operands follow GNU's messages and status.
cases.script:
ln --bogus a b || echo rc=$?
ln -Z a b || echo rc=$?
ln -s || echo rc=$?
ln -T a || echo rc=$?
printf x > a; ln a b c || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: -L hard-links a symlink's referent; -P (the default) links the symlink itself.
cases.script:
printf x > target
ln -s target sym
ln -L sym hl
ln -P sym hp
[[ hl -ef target ]] && echo L-ok
[[ -L hp ]] && readlink hp

cases.purpose: Guest compatibility pass 2 (G38): `--help` prints help on stdout and exits 0, as GNU tools do, for ln and the other builtins fixed with it.
cases.script:
for c in ln mktemp cp sort tail wc tr xargs stat mkdir chmod uniq; do
  $c --help >o 2>e; r=$?
  [[ $r == 0 && -s o && ! -s e ]] && echo "$c ok" || echo "$c rc=$r"
done
cases.stdout:
ln ok
mktemp ok
cp ok
sort ok
tail ok
wc ok
tr ok
xargs ok
stat ok
mkdir ok
chmod ok
uniq ok

cases.purpose: Docker parity errors/ln: an invalid or ambiguous --backup argument, or a bad VERSION_CONTROL, lists the valid keywords before the Try line; unique prefixes are accepted. The rejected calls run in a scratch directory that is removed: GNU coreutils 9.7 ln (and mv) still make the link after this fatal-looking diagnostic and exit 1, while bash-os stops; that side effect is a recorded, deliberate difference, the diagnostics and statuses are compared here.
cases.script:
touch a
mkdir t
ln --backup=bad a t/b || echo "rc=$?"
ln --backup=n a t/b || echo "rc=$?"
VERSION_CONTROL=bad ln -b a t/c || echo "rc=$?"
rm -r t
ln --backup=nu a d || echo "rc=$?"
ln --backup=nu a d || echo "rc=$?"
ln -S .x --backup=s a e || echo "rc=$?"
ln -S .x --backup=s a e || echo "rc=$?"
ls
